description: A persistent, non‑infectious inflammation of the conjunctiva driven by allergic mechanisms, characterized by chronic itching, redness, and tearing.
Inflammation of the right upper eyelid margin of unspecified etiology.
Meibomian gland dysfunction of the right upper eyelid is a chronic disorder characterized by obstruction of the meibomian glands leading to altered tear film and ocular surface irritation.
Neonatal conjunctivitis and dacryocystitis are acute bacterial infections of the eye and lacrimal sac occurring within the first month of life.
Zoster scleritis is an acute inflammatory condition of the sclera caused by reactivation of varicella‑zoster virus, often presenting with severe eye pain and vision loss.
A nonspecific ocular pain affecting either eye without a clearly identified underlying cause.
Acute ocular pain localized to the right eye, often accompanied by redness, tearing, and photophobia, indicating a potential inflammatory or traumatic ocular condition.
Localized pain in the left eye, often accompanied by inflammation, irritation, or increased intraocular pressure.

Acute follicular conjunctivitis, bilateral is a rapidly developing inflammation of both conjunctival surfaces characterized by follicle formation, redness, itching, tearing, and mild to moderate discharge.
Acute inflammation of the lacrimal sac due to obstruction of the right nasolacrimal duct.
Glare sensitivity is a visual disturbance characterized by discomfort and impaired vision when exposed to bright light.
A bilateral retinal condition characterized by neovascularization in the absence of diabetes, leading to potential vision loss.

Nonexudative age‑related macular degeneration is a chronic, progressive retinal disease characterized by the accumulation of drusen and atrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium, leading to gradual loss of central vision.
Unilateral visual loss in the right eye with normal vision in the left eye, not meeting criteria for qualified visual impairment.

Unqualified visual loss in the left eye with normal vision in the right eye is a unilateral visual impairment presenting as sudden or gradual loss of sight in the left eye while the right eye remains unaffected.
Primary open-angle glaucoma is a chronic optic neuropathy characterized by progressive, painless loss of peripheral vision due to elevated intraocular pressure.
